tomato___septoria_leaf_spot.name: Septoria Leaf Spot
symptoms: Small circular dark grey spots with dark borders on lower leaves
Tiny black pycnidia dots visible inside spot centers
Yellowing (chlorosis) of surrounding leaf tissue leading to premature defoliation

cultural: Enforce 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops
Mulch soil bed with straw to prevent fungal spore splash-back from soil
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; install drip lines
mechanical: Prune and destroy infected lower leaves up to 12 inches above soil line
Stake plants vertically to facilitate maximum airflow canopy aeration
biological: Apply Trichoderma harzianum or Bacillus subtilis foliar spray weekly
chemical: CAUTION: Apply preventive Copper Oxychloride (2.5g/L) or Mancozeb (2g/L). Rotate mode-of-action FRAC codes to prevent fungal resistance.

tomato___septoria_leaf_spot.expertEscalation: Contact local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) if leaf defoliation exceeds 30% of canopy.

tomato___blossom_end_rot.name: Blossom End Rot
symptoms: Water-soaked dark leathery sunken patch at bottom (blossom end) of developing fruit
Dry black flattened area expanding as fruit ripens

cultural: Maintain consistent, uniform soil moisture; avoid drastic wet-dry irrigation cycles
Apply organic compost or lime to adjust soil pH to 6.2 - 6.8 for optimal Calcium uptake
mechanical: Prune non-productive sucker branches to divert transpiration stream to fruits
biological: Foliar spray of Calcium Nitrate (0.5%) during early fruit set
chemical: Not a pathogen. Do NOT apply fungicides. Correct soil moisture and Calcium balance.

tomato___blossom_end_rot.expertEscalation: Conduct soil EC & Calcium analysis if over 15% of green set shows rot.

tomato___healthy.name: Healthy Tomato Canopy
symptoms: Vibrant green leaves free from chlorosis or foliar lesions
Sturdy stem development and normal flowering set

cultural: Maintain balanced N-P-K nutrition and routine weeding.
biological: Preventive neem oil spray (5ml/L) as general repellent.

rice___leaf_blast.name: Rice Leaf Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae)
symptoms: Spindle-shaped or diamond-shaped lesions with reddish-brown margins and grey center
Lesion enlargement causing leaf blade wilting and complete foliage browning

cultural: Maintain standing water depth (5-7cm) during tillering stage to suppress spore infection
mechanical: Remove and burn infected stubble post-harvest
biological: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/kg seed)
chemical: CAUTION: Apply Tricyclazole 75 WP (0.6g/L) or Isoprothiolane 40 EC (1.5ml/L) at early lesion appearance.

rice___leaf_blast.expertEscalation: Immediate escalation required if neck blast phase is observed at panicle emergence.

rice___healthy.name: Healthy Rice Field
symptoms: Uniform green tiller canopy without foliar spots or yellowing

cultural: Standard water management and balanced nitrogen split dosage.

wheat___yellow_rust.name: Wheat Yellow Rust (Puccinia striiformis)
symptoms: Bright yellow powdery urediniospores arranged in distinct linear stripes along leaf veins
Premature leaf drying leading to grain shriveling

cultural: Sow rust-resistant varieties recommended by ICAR (e.g. HD-3086, DBW-187)
Timely sowing before winter temperature drop
biological: Bio-formulations of Bacillus subtilis foliar spray
chemical: CAUTION: Spray Propiconazole 25 EC (1ml/L) or Tebuconazole 50% + Trifloxystrobin 25% WG at first sign of yellow stripe.

wheat___yellow_rust.expertEscalation: Notify District Agriculture Officer immediately upon yellow rust stripe outbreak.

wheat___healthy.name: Healthy Wheat Field
symptoms: Vibrant green leaf blades free from yellow stripes or foliar pustules
